name: Hydrafacial Keravive

lead: Keravive, also marketed as HydraScalp, is a clinic scalp treatment that cleanses, exfoliates and applies serums to the scalp. It is pitched for scalp health and hair quality, including for thinning hair.

A handheld device performs the cleansing and exfoliation and delivers topical products, adapting the brand's multi-step facial platform for the scalp. A 44-person study in androgenetic alopecia is listed as completed, and a 15-person study pairing a scalp serum with the treatment in people with self-perceived thinning is registered; no results were found.

paras: It is a salon or clinic session, sometimes paired with a scalp serum.
No safety data were found in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: It is pitched as a salon scalp facial: cleansing and exfoliation plus serums delivered to the scalp for a healthier-looking scalp and better hair quality. The hair claim comes from marketing; two registered studies exist with no published results.

lead: Hydrafacial Keravive, also marketed as HydraScalp, is a salon and clinic scalp treatment from the Hydrafacial brand that adapts its multi-step facial platform to the scalp. It cleanses and exfoliates the scalp, applies peptide-containing serums and is marketed to people with thinning hair or a dry, itchy, congested scalp, with the goal of a healthier scalp and hair that looks fuller and shinier. [1][2]

The company describes three steps: purify (light suction and exfoliation to open the follicles), nourish (peptides and hydration applied to the cleansed follicles) and boost (a daily take-home peptide spray). [2] It recommends a series, usually three treatments about a month apart, with each session taking roughly 30 to 60 minutes depending on whether the whole scalp is treated. [2]

Hydrafacial states the treatment is clinically proven to help reduce hair thinning, citing a pilot study run by the company, in which 75% of participants reported improved hair fullness after one treatment and 82% reported shinier, healthier-looking hair by the third visit. [2] Independent published results are not yet available; two studies are registered, one completed in androgenetic alopecia. [1][3]

paras: The treatment applies Hydrafacial's approach of cleansing, exfoliating and infusing products, here to the scalp. [2] Per the company, it is marketed to men and women with hair loss, thinning or poor scalp health, and is described as suitable for all scalp and hair types, including braids, extensions, locks and dyed hair. Providers may recommend it alongside other hair restoration or scalp treatments. [2]

Hydrafacial reports that after three monthly treatments plus daily spray use, users described a smoother scalp with less itching, reduced hair loss and thinning, and hair that looks and feels thicker. [2] The company notes that the cited results come from company-sponsored studies and testimonials, and that individual results vary. [2]

NCT06112782, "Keravive by Hydrafacial for Scalp Health and Enhanced Hair Quality," enrolled 44 participants with androgenetic alopecia, began in July 2019 and is listed as completed; no peer-reviewed results were located. [3]
NCT07935993 is planned to begin in November 2026 with 15 participants with self-perceived hair thinning, testing a scalp serum paired with the HydraScalp Keravive treatment. [1]

timeline.event: A study of Keravive for scalp health and hair quality in androgenetic alopecia starts. [3]
A trial pairing a scalp serum with the treatment is registered for people with hair thinning. [1]
